questions.question: Explain how an undergravel filter works. Why is it considered less effective in modern aquariums?
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how an undergravel filter works. Why is it considered less effective in
  • modern aquariums? /
  • An undergravel filter (UGF) is a biological filtration system placed beneath the
  • aquarium substrate (gravel). Uplift tubes, Air pumps or powerheads , suction, pulling
  • water down through the gravel , beneficial bacteria colonize the substrate ,
  • Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter These bacteria convert toxic ammonia → nitrite → nitrate
  • (biological filtration), Filtered water then rises up through the uplift tubes
  • Less effective in modern aquariums : Accumulation of waste , Difficult maintenance,
  • Limited filtration efficiency , Not suitable for pla nted tanks , Inflexibility, Better
  • alternatives available (canister filter etc.)
questions.final_answer: alternatives available (canister filter etc.)

questions.solution_html:
• What is mechanical filtration? Explain its working principle, examples and benefits./
  • Definition: a process that physically removes solid waste and particulate matter (like uneaten food,
  • fish waste, and debris) from aquarium water by trapping it in a filter medium.
  • Working Principle: Aquarium water drawn through filter by pump or gravity and as it passes
  • through the filter medium(sponge , pads or floss), solid particles are trapped and clear water returned
  • to the Aquarium.
questions.final_answer: to the Aquarium.
